title: Composing Global Solutions to Reasoning Tasks via Algebraic Objects in Neural Nets
abstract: This paper introduces a framework for composing global solutions to reasoning tasks using algebraic objects in neural networks. The framework, called CoGS, enables the construction of global solutions from partial solutions that satisfy only part of the loss function.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a puzzle, but instead of using trial and error, you can use algebraic structures to find the solution. This is the core idea behind CoGS, which uses algebraic objects in neural networks to compose global solutions to reasoning tasks.

By leveraging the algebraic structure of the solution space, we can construct global solutions from partial solutions, making it possible to solve complex tasks more efficiently.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
CoGS works by defining a semi-ring structure over the weight space of a 2-layer neural network. This structure allows us to compose partial solutions using ring addition and multiplication, resulting in global solutions that satisfy the entire loss function.

The key to this approach is the use of sum potentials, which are ring homomorphisms that enable the composition of partial solutions.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
Our experiments show that around 95% of the solutions obtained by gradient descent match exactly our theoretical constructions. This demonstrates the effectiveness of CoGS in composing global solutions to reasoning tasks.

We also show that the dynamics of sum potentials become decoupled with infinite width, which helps to explain why overparameterization improves performance.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
CoGS has significant implications for the field of artificial intelligence, as it provides a new framework for solving complex reasoning tasks. By leveraging algebraic structures, we can construct global solutions more efficiently, which can lead to breakthroughs in areas such as natural language processing and computer vision.

Additionally, CoGS provides new insights into the dynamics of neural networks, which can help us better understand how they work and how to improve their performance.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
The key innovations of CoGS are the use of algebraic structures to compose global solutions and the definition of sum potentials as ring homomorphisms. These innovations enable the construction of global solutions from partial solutions, making it possible to solve complex tasks more efficiently.

Additionally, CoGS provides new insights into the dynamics of neural networks, which can help us better understand how they work and how to improve their performance.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
To try CoGS yourself, you can use the open-sourced code provided in the paper. The code includes implementations of the CoGS framework and examples of how to use it to solve reasoning tasks.

By experimenting with CoGS, you can gain a deeper understanding of how it works and how to apply it to your own research and projects.
